# Undisclosed

> Undisclosed is an open source, local-first AI coding editor. It is a customized
> Eclipse Theia editor with an AI coding agent built in as a native dock panel
> instead of a separate window. The agent plans, edits, runs commands and tests
> against your real workspace. The editor and the agent backend ("the brain", a
> local FastAPI service) both run on the user's machine. Models are either local
> (Ollama, LM Studio, Hugging Face) or cloud models reached with the user's own
> API key (BYOK), including DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google Gemini and Mistral.

- License: Apache-2.0
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, Linux (Electron desktop builds; unsigned for now)
- Source: https://github.com/Octagon-simon/undisclosed
- Releases: https://github.com/Octagon-simon/undisclosed/releases
- Issues: https://github.com/Octagon-simon/undisclosed/issues
- Website: the static landing page in the repository's `site/` folder

## What it is

An editor-first product, not a chat app with a code viewer bolted on. The editor
shell is our own build on top of Eclipse Theia 1.76 (Monaco, terminal, git,
debugging, search, VS Code settings and Open VSX extension import). The agent
capability comes from Eigent AI and is fused into the editor as a first-class
dock widget, opened with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A.

Two local processes:

1. Editor: Theia plus the `undisclosed-*` extensions and the embedded agent
   panel. Dev server on port 3000; packaged as an Electron desktop app.
2. Brain: FastAPI/uvicorn agent backend on port 5001 for model routing, tools
   ("hands"), memory and streaming.

They talk over localhost. In the packaged app, Electron starts and stops the
brain alongside the editor.

## Models

- Local, on the user's hardware: Ollama, LM Studio, Hugging Face.
- Cloud, BYOK: DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, and any
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Keys are configured in the app's Models UI or in
  `.env`.
- The model is chosen per task; there is no Undisclosed-hosted model and no
  mandatory account.

## What the agent can do

- Plan a change and show the plan as a card before writing.
- Read and write files, run terminal commands, search the repo.
- Use git, debugging, a browser, screenshots and web search.
- Run the tests for the files it changed and show a test-run receipt (passed,
  failed, duration). The receipt only appears when the run happened after the
  turn's last file edit.
- Publish and review diffs file by file.
- Create and comment on GitHub issues and pull requests when a token is set.
- Notify the user on the desktop, or in Slack when connected, when it finishes
  or needs input.

## Skills

A skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter (name,
description) and instructions. The agent loads a skill only when a task matches
it, so installed skills do not inflate every prompt. Twenty skills ship with the
app (frontend, design, accessibility, anti-slop UI, decks). More, including
HyperFrames video skills, media tools, Figma and document skills, install from
their upstream GitHub repositories by pasting a URL into the agent. See
https://github.com/Octagon-simon/undisclosed/blob/upgrade/theia-1.76/docs/extra-skills.md

## Privacy model

- The editor and the agent brain run on the user's machine. The brain binds
  `127.0.0.1:5001` by default.
- There is no Undisclosed account and no analytics SDK in the app.
- With a local model, the whole loop works offline and no code leaves the
  machine.
- With a BYOK cloud model, the prompt and the context the agent sends go to that
  provider. Nothing passes through an Undisclosed server.
- Conversation turns are stored in `~/.undisclosed/turns`, memory in
  `~/.undisclosed/memory`, and brain logs in `~/.undisclosed/logs`. Debug dumps
  are opt-in with `UNDISCLOSED_DEBUG=1`. The Memory panel can switch memory off
  or clear stored facts.
- Approval mode defaults to Ask. Terminal commands that change files, file
  writes and deletions, and git add/commit wait for an explicit prompt that
  names the action; a denial or five-minute timeout stops it. Auto is opt-in and
  lets ordinary workspace edits run without asking.
- Commands that can wipe data or take over the host (`rm`, `sudo`, `dd`,
  `mkfs`, `fdisk`, `shutdown`, `find -delete`, `xargs rm`) are hard-blocked in
  every mode, and approval cannot override the block. A script that deletes a
  literal path outside the workspace is blocked; one whose delete target is a
  variable or glob prompts in every mode. `git push`, `git reset`, `git clean`
  and GitHub writes prompt in every mode.
- Deletion inside the workspace is allowed when the task requires it: the
  `delete_files` tool takes explicit paths and refuses the workspace root,
  `.git`, `..` escapes and symlinks that point outside.
- Integrations stay unavailable until connected. GitHub writes prompt in every
  mode; the MongoDB write escape hatch is gated in Ask. Slack, Notion and Google
  connectors are not gated yet, so their tokens should be scoped to what the
  agent may touch.

## Reliability

- Every code change goes through the same loop before the agent reports it done:
  `run_checks` (project typecheck and lint), `review_diff` (deterministic,
  line-anchored findings, no extra model call), and `run_tests` with a
  coverage-gap plan the agent has to address or explain.
- The panel keeps the receipts for the turn: the file diff, the test-run card
  and the verification summary.
- Success is judged on real tasks: tests pass, the diff matches the request, how
  often the agent needed intervention, and how much manual correction was
  required. Tool count is not a score.
- The evaluation currently runs on this repository and on Angler. There is no
  public leaderboard yet.

## Built with Undisclosed

- Undisclosed itself: the editor, agent panel, brain, README and the demo video
  rendered inside it.
- Angler (https://getanglerapp.com): a macOS menu-bar app that gives the flat
  desktop depth as the laptop lid tilts. App and site built with Undisclosed.

## Demo

A 35 second demo shows one task end to end in the app: a request for a
`slugify()` function, the plan card, the git diff across two files, and a pytest
run with 9 passing tests. It is served at /demo.mp4 on this site. The video was
cut, captioned and rendered inside Undisclosed using the HyperFrames skill.

## Common questions

- Do I need an API key? No. A local model works without one.
- Does it work offline? Yes, with a local model. The editor and brain are local
  either way.
- Is it a VS Code fork? No. It is built on Eclipse Theia.
- Is it free? The app is Apache-2.0. Cloud model usage is billed by the provider
  the user chooses.

## Preferred description

"Undisclosed is an open source, local-first AI coding editor built on Eclipse
Theia. Its agent lives inside the editor and can plan, edit, run tests and
report back, using local models or the user's own cloud model keys."
